method: Each edge is projected onto the spherical Web Mercator plane (EPSG:3857): x = (longitude + 180) / 360, and y = (1 - ln(tan(pi/4 + phi/2)) / pi) / 2, with phi the latitude in radians clamped to the +/-85.0511287798066 degree limit where the projection is finite. The box width is the eastward longitude difference divided by 360, taken through 180 degrees when west is larger than east, and the box height is the difference of the two y values. At zoom z the world is tile size x 2^z pixels across, so the box spans box width x tile x 2^z pixels horizontally and box height x tile x 2^z vertically. The exact fit zoom is the smaller of log2(viewport width / (box width x tile size)) and log2(viewport height / (box height x tile size)); that value is rounded down to a whole zoom, with a one-part-in-a-billion tolerance so an exact fit stays at its own zoom, and clamped to the usual 0 to 22 range. At the chosen zoom the page reports the box centre (the wrapped midpoint of the x range and the midpoint of the y range inverted back to latitude), the box size in screen pixels, the ground resolution at the centre 40075016.68557849 m x cos(centre latitude) / world width, the map scale denominator at 96 dpi (metres per pixel divided by 0.0254/96), and the tile columns and rows covering the box, with a one-part-in-a-billion tolerance so an edge that sits exactly on a tile boundary does not add an empty row or column. Inputs are refused outside -90 to 90 degrees latitude, -180 to 180 degrees longitude, a viewport of 1 to 10000 whole pixels and the 256 or 512 pixel tile sizes; north must be greater than south, west and east must differ, and a box that collapses to zero height after clamping is refused. Decimal commas are accepted. The page does not reproject to other datums or projections, report resolution anywhere but the box centre, know about terrain, tilt, padding, tile overlap or retina tile sets beyond the tile-size choice, and it does not fetch or draw any map. It runs entirely in the browser with no storage, uploads or network access.

sources.title: Wikipedia, Web Mercator projection: the spherical projection normalises longitude and a stretched latitude, and is only finite up to about 85.0511 degrees, the clamp this page applies.
OpenStreetMap Wiki, Slippy map tilenames: a zoom level z splits the world into 2^z by 2^z tiles of 256 pixels, so the world is 256 x 2^z pixels wide and a viewport fit follows from that ratio.
Wikipedia, Scale (map): map scale is a ratio of map distance to ground distance, computed here from the ground resolution at the box centre with 96 CSS pixels to the inch.
